comments.author: @RemoteEarthJourneys
comments.text: What surprised me most about Bermuda wasn’t the beaches — it was how much daily life is shaped by having so little land. The white roofs collecting rainwater, limits on cars, imported food prices, and young people leaving for college all make the island feel completely different from the postcard version most of us know. If you actually live in Bermuda, what’s one thing outsiders almost always misunderstand about everyday life there?
